name: a-his-shadow-arrives-first
prompt: A hand-carved relief print pulled in two inks, burnt rust-orange and dense black, on rough cream paper with visible wood grain in the solid areas and slightly off registration between the colours. Every line is gouged and splintered, cut by a knife rather than drawn, with no soft shading, only hacked black against bare orange. The viewpoint lies almost on the ground of a gravel park path in 1919, the rubber-capped tip of a wooden crutch filling the lower corner of the frame up close, and the whole picture tilted a few degrees off level so the path runs uphill and away. Far up the path, small and sharp at the top third of the frame, a park bench: on it a fat rich man in a tall silk top hat, frock coat and waistcoat, one gloved hand lifted in a bored backhanded flick of dismissal, and beside him a thin young soldier in a worn army tunic, one trouser leg pinned up empty at the knee. A low sunset sits directly behind the bench, a blazing orange disc cut with radiating chisel strokes, so that the rich man's shadow pours toward the viewer down the gravel, monstrously long and swollen, the top hat stretched into a black tower and the belly into a bloated mass, bending over the soldier and swallowing the path right up to the crutch tip. The soldier's own shadow is a thin broken sliver beside it. Bare twisted trees lean inward at the edges. The upper fifth of the frame is an empty band of streaked orange sky with nothing in it. No words, letters or numbers anywhere in the image. Thanks.
